audit.verification: One real building with two verified Los Angeles-set appearances, not a list of every production credit. Larry Crowne: Visit Burbank and IAMNOTASTALKER independently identify scooter-group lunches and the cook job; Levy explicitly calls the movie set in and around Los Angeles, and The National describes the scooter gang cruising suburban Los Angeles.

Scorpion: Gary Wayne’s frame guide matches Frank’s interior to the pilot’s Paige/Ralph/Walter scenes and later emergency base. The aired transcript names the L.A. office, LAX/Long Beach/Burbank airports and Los Angeles infrastructure; the development screenplay explicitly labels the diner Los Angeles. Development-draft distances and Paige’s superseded surname were not treated as final continuity.

Coordinates are the Census Public_AR_Current street-interpolated match for 916 W OLIVE AVE, BURBANK, CA, 91506, retrieved November 16, 2026. They identify the production address, not a proven canonical street number.
Canonical years c.2011 and c.2014 are contemporary release-year estimates, not exact dates. Date filtering must retain these dated estimates.

Visually inspected source images: Larry scooter-group exterior, Larry kitchen frame, Scorpion diner-counter scene and wide rescue-base scene, 2020 exterior and 2021 window/interior photo. Public files use the exterior Larry frame and wide Scorpion frame. Only black letterbox bars and the 1px source border were removed; no image was generated.

Real-site primary photo is published June 8, 2020; capture date is not asserted. Additional file photos/f224-2021-place.jpg is Ian / Flickr’s photograph with embedded page dateTaken 2021-06-06 12:09:10, showing the closed sign through the window; its source is franks_real_2021. No current operating status is claimed.

No scene-specific, canonically Los Angeles evidence was established for the suggested Lucifer, Bosch, Barry, Casual, Goliath, Fast & Furious, Mad Men or True Romance leads. Review’s pancake scene is a credible Frank’s lead but story geography remains unverified. These are research holds, not assertions that the productions never used Frank’s.

excluded.title: Beverly Hills, 90210 · Squash It
excluded.reason: The Frank’s exterior represents a diner near Reno, Nevada; Valerie meets Ray there before returning to Beverly Hills. A different restaurant supplied the interior.

excluded.title: CSI: Crime Scene Investigation
excluded.reason: Identified diner scenes belong to the Las Vegas story, including Rashomama, Law of Gravity, Mascara and The List. Los Angeles production does not make them Los Angeles story locations.

excluded.title: Parks and Recreation · Ron and Tammy
excluded.reason: Ron and Tammy’s lunch is in the Pawnee, Indiana story.

excluded.title: Gone Girl
excluded.reason: Nick, Margo and Tanner’s diner consultation is part of the Missouri investigation, not the film’s New York backstory or a Los Angeles scene.

excluded.title: Weird: The Al Yankovic Story
excluded.reason: Although Al’s home/career has Los Angeles scenes, the Frank’s kidnapping/fight follows the Miami-Dade concert arrest and jail release into a late-night diner. Screenplay scenes 56–58 establish the Miami context.

excluded.title: Gigli
excluded.reason: The Frank’s scene is verified in a trailer but the scene guide could not find it in the released film; hold until a released-version appearance is demonstrated.

excluded.title: Euphoria · Trouble Don’t Last Always
excluded.reason: Rue and Ali’s Frank’s scene is verified, but its fictional East Highland setting has not been established as Los Angeles County by a canonical source. Held rather than treating filming geography as story geography.
